Audited against `gerrit-sora/develop` only.

**BLOCKER**

- `[PROMOTE] BLOCKER — default promote registry is the wrong registry/path: script defaults to `sora.services:49154/omnisight/OmniSight-Productizer`, while ADR/readiness say sole prod registry is `sora.services:49160/omnisight/omnisight-productizer`; an operator who omits `--registry` promotes into the wrong CR namespace — scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:51, scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:627 — violates: ADR-0042:20, docs/operations/2026-05-22-release-train-readiness-handoff.md:12`

- `[PROD] BLOCKER — digest deploy path is advertised but not wired: `deploy-prod.sh --digest` writes `OMNISIGHT_IMAGE_DIGEST`, then sets `OMNISIGHT_IMAGE_TAG` to the digest; prod compose ignores `OMNISIGHT_IMAGE_DIGEST` and uses tag syntax, so digest deploy either renders an invalid image ref or deploys the old tag — scripts/deploy-prod.sh:255, scripts/deploy-prod.sh:264, scripts/deploy-prod.sh:278, docker-compose.prod.yml:152 — violates: ADR-0040:36, ADR-0040:82`

- `[PROD] BLOCKER — legacy `ProductionDeployOrchestrator.ship()` does not deploy the requested tag through compose: it exports `OMNISIGHT_RELEASE_IMAGE_TAG`, but compose consumes `OMNISIGHT_IMAGE_TAG`; it may pull `<tag>` then `up` whatever `.env` already says — backend/production_release.py:281, backend/production_release.py:292, docker-compose.prod.yml:152 — violates: ADR-0040:34, docs/operations/2026-05-22-release-train-readiness-handoff.md:36`

- `[PROD] BLOCKER — prod deploy API is effectively dead code: router defines `POST /prod/deploy`, but `backend/main.py` mounts health/release/audit routers and never mounts `backend.orchestrator.prod_deploy.router`; tests mount it manually — backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:509, backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:512, backend/main.py:1402, backend/main.py:1559, backend/main.py:1628 — violates: backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:3`

- `[COSIGN] BLOCKER — GitLab CI key-based signing/attestation omits `--tlog-upload=false`; private promotion/build metadata can leak to Rekor despite the runbook saying private/no Rekor leak — .gitlab-ci.yml:404, .gitlab-ci.yml:466, .gitlab-ci.yml:497, .gitlab-ci.yml:550 — violates: docs/operations/2026-05-22-release-train-readiness-handoff.md:55`

- `[ADR] BLOCKER — GHCR is not decommissioned: active GitHub workflows still push/build GHCR on `develop`, `main`, and `v*` tags; this also reintroduces forbidden `v*` git-tag release builds — .github/workflows/build-images.yml:29, .github/workflows/build-images.yml:58, .github/workflows/build-images.yml:181, .github/workflows/build-images.yml:229, .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:17, .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:35 — violates: ADR-0042:20, ADR-0042:21, ADR-0040:34`

**HIGH**

- `[PROMOTE] HIGH — escape hatches can promote unverified/unstaged images with no production guard and no audit flag: `--skip-staging-gate` and `--skip-cosign-verify` are only help-text restricted; audit row does not record either bypass — scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:642, scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:650, scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:675, scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:677, scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:431 — violates: ADR-0040:36, ADR-0040:85`

- `[PROMOTE] HIGH — audit row is a mutable local JSONL file, not the ADR release identity row; no hash chain, no DB write, no fsync, and it is written after registry retag/sign side effects, so “audit write aborts promote” cannot undo a promoted tag — scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:414, scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:453, scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:548 — violates: ADR-0040:34, ADR-0040:90`

- `[PROMOTE] HIGH — staging evidence is weakly bound: malformed JSONL lines are silently ignored, records with `bundle_id: null` can authorize any bundle, and only two digest fields plus `status` are checked; no evidence signature/hash/attestation linkage — scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:249, scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:255, scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:270, scripts/promote_image_bundle.py:276 — violates: ADR-0040:36, docs/operations/2026-05-22-release-train-readiness-handoff.md:21`

- `[COSIGN] HIGH — `sign_promotion_attestation.py` falls back to keyless OIDC when `COSIGN_KEY` is unset; `--tlog-upload=false` is only added in the key path, so a missing env silently changes trust/privacy mode — scripts/sign_promotion_attestation.py:8, scripts/sign_promotion_attestation.py:79, scripts/sign_promotion_attestation.py:83 — violates: docs/operations/2026-05-22-release-train-readiness-handoff.md:52`

- `[COSIGN] HIGH — `build_image.sh` still has stale registry/key defaults and signs without `--tlog-upload=false`; docs explicitly warn the key path is stale — scripts/build_image.sh:26, scripts/build_image.sh:29, scripts/build_image.sh:202 — violates: ADR-0042:20, docs/operations/2026-05-22-release-train-readiness-handoff.md:57`

- `[PROD] HIGH — orchestrator’s “dual approval” is not a real Slack gate by default; it accepts any token from an env allowlist, not a Slack bridge/DM verification — backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:202, backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:212 — violates: backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:11`

- `[PROD] HIGH — orchestrator smoke check defaults to `http://staging-mirror.internal:8080`, with no evidence this endpoint exists; the default production path is a stub endpoint — backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:159, backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:162 — violates: backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:7`

- `[PROD] HIGH — orchestrator “blue-green switch” only delegates to the broken legacy `ship()` path, inheriting its env/tag bug and rollback weaknesses — backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:166, backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:171 — violates: backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:9`

- `[FAIL-CLOSED] HIGH — deploy-overlay gate is documented as prod/staging fail-closed, but neither prod nor staging compose sets `OMNISIGHT_REQUIRE_DEPLOY_OVERLAY`; health only fails closed when that env is set — backend/routers/health.py:466, backend/routers/health.py:477, backend/routers/health.py:488, deploy/staging/docker-compose.yml:102, docker-compose.prod.yml:170 — violates: ADR-0040:92, docs/operations/2026-05-22-release-train-readiness-handoff.md:20`

- `[ADR] HIGH — `main` is not retired: active workflows still trigger on `main`, and live code paths still default/push to `refs/for/main` — .github/workflows/ci.yml:5, .github/workflows/image-build.yml:18, backend/agents/auto_promote_main.py:211, backend/agents/auto_promote_main.py:412, deploy/systemd/auto-promote-develop.service:5 — violates: ADR-0040:32, ADR-0040:33, ADR-0040:80`

**MED**

- `[PROD] MED — manual deploy backup fails open if `scripts/backup_prod_db.sh` is missing; production deploy continues “WITHOUT backup” — scripts/deploy-prod.sh:303, scripts/deploy-prod.sh:306, scripts/deploy-prod.sh:309 — violates: fail-closed deployment safety expectations`

- `[PROD] MED — manual smoke test checks only `localhost:8000/api/v1/health`; it does not verify backend-b, frontend, Caddy/TLS, or public ingress after the rollout — scripts/deploy-prod.sh:425, scripts/deploy-prod.sh:430 — violates: ADR-0040:82`

- `[PROD] MED — legacy rollback is not image rollback; `ship()` calls `scripts/deploy.sh --rollback`, unrelated to release-train previous tag/digest rollback and after migrations may already have run — backend/production_release.py:286, backend/production_release.py:319 — violates: ADR-0040:59, ADR-0040:77`

- `[FAIL-CLOSED] MED — frontend compatibility gate is claimed to be staging-enforced, but compose does not set `OMNISIGHT_REQUIRE_FRONTEND_COMPAT`; it remains observational unless hidden `.env` happens to provide it — backend/routers/health.py:518, backend/routers/health.py:720, deploy/staging/docker-compose.yml:102 — violates: ADR-0040:82`

- `[ADR] MED — prod compose still documents an emergency GHCR fallback after ADR-0042 says GHCR is decommissioned and GitLab CR is sole registry — docker-compose.prod.yml:17, docker-compose.prod.yml:31 — violates: ADR-0042:20, ADR-0042:21`

- `[ADR] MED — `.env.example` is stale/contradictory: it documents `${OMNISIGHT_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}` while prod compose now requires `OMNISIGHT_IMAGE_TAG`; this can mislead operators about fail-closed tag behavior — .env.example:154, .env.example:166, docker-compose.prod.yml:152 — violates: ADR-0040:62`

**LOW**

- `[COSIGN] LOW — signature verifier examples still use GHCR paths, encouraging the wrong registry in operator muscle memory — scripts/verify_image_signature.sh:8, scripts/verify_image_signature.sh:27 — violates: ADR-0042:20`

- `[ADR] LOW — stale ops docs still instruct `git checkout main` / GHCR-era release flow, contradicting the release train model — docs/operations/release-cut-runbook.md:22, docs/operations/deployment-master-runbook.md:174 — violates: ADR-0040:33`

**Verdict:** pipeline health is not production-trustworthy: promote-by-digest has the right core digest-equality idea, but registry drift, bypassable gates, non-authoritative audit, broken prod deploy wiring, live GHCR/main residue, and missing fail-closed env wiring mean the dev→prod chain is currently easy to misdeploy or falsely attest.

- `[PROD] HIGH — orchestrator smoke check defaults to `http://staging-mirror.internal:8080`, with no evidence this endpoint exists; the default production path is a stub endpoint — backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:159, backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:162 — violates: backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:7`

- `[PROD] HIGH — orchestrator “blue-green switch” only delegates to the broken legacy `ship()` path, inheriting its env/tag bug and rollback weaknesses — backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:166, backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:171 — violates: backend/orchestrator/prod_deploy.py:9`

- `[FAIL-CLOSED] HIGH — deploy-overlay gate is documented as prod/staging fail-closed, but neither prod nor staging compose sets `OMNISIGHT_REQUIRE_DEPLOY_OVERLAY`; health only fails closed when that env is set — backend/routers/health.py:466, backend/routers/health.py:477, backend/routers/health.py:488, deploy/staging/docker-compose.yml:102, docker-compose.prod.yml:170 — violates: ADR-0040:92, docs/operations/2026-05-22-release-train-readiness-handoff.md:20`

- `[ADR] HIGH — `main` is not retired: active workflows still trigger on `main`, and live code paths still default/push to `refs/for/main` — .github/workflows/ci.yml:5, .github/workflows/image-build.yml:18, backend/agents/auto_promote_main.py:211, backend/agents/auto_promote_main.py:412, deploy/systemd/auto-promote-develop.service:5 — violates: ADR-0040:32, ADR-0040:33, ADR-0040:80`

**MED**

- `[PROD] MED — manual deploy backup fails open if `scripts/backup_prod_db.sh` is missing; production deploy continues “WITHOUT backup” — scripts/deploy-prod.sh:303, scripts/deploy-prod.sh:306, scripts/deploy-prod.sh:309 — violates: fail-closed deployment safety expectations`

- `[PROD] MED — manual smoke test checks only `localhost:8000/api/v1/health`; it does not verify backend-b, frontend, Caddy/TLS, or public ingress after the rollout — scripts/deploy-prod.sh:425, scripts/deploy-prod.sh:430 — violates: ADR-0040:82`

- `[PROD] MED — legacy rollback is not image rollback; `ship()` calls `scripts/deploy.sh --rollback`, unrelated to release-train previous tag/digest rollback and after migrations may already have run — backend/production_release.py:286, backend/production_release.py:319 — violates: ADR-0040:59, ADR-0040:77`

- `[FAIL-CLOSED] MED — frontend compatibility gate is claimed to be staging-enforced, but compose does not set `OMNISIGHT_REQUIRE_FRONTEND_COMPAT`; it remains observational unless hidden `.env` happens to provide it — backend/routers/health.py:518, backend/routers/health.py:720, deploy/staging/docker-compose.yml:102 — violates: ADR-0040:82`

- `[ADR] MED — prod compose still documents an emergency GHCR fallback after ADR-0042 says GHCR is decommissioned and GitLab CR is sole registry — docker-compose.prod.yml:17, docker-compose.prod.yml:31 — violates: ADR-0042:20, ADR-0042:21`

- `[ADR] MED — `.env.example` is stale/contradictory: it documents `${OMNISIGHT_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}` while prod compose now requires `OMNISIGHT_IMAGE_TAG`; this can mislead operators about fail-closed tag behavior — .env.example:154, .env.example:166, docker-compose.prod.yml:152 — violates: ADR-0040:62`

**LOW**

- `[COSIGN] LOW — signature verifier examples still use GHCR paths, encouraging the wrong registry in operator muscle memory — scripts/verify_image_signature.sh:8, scripts/verify_image_signature.sh:27 — violates: ADR-0042:20`

- `[ADR] LOW — stale ops docs still instruct `git checkout main` / GHCR-era release flow, contradicting the release train model — docs/operations/release-cut-runbook.md:22, docs/operations/deployment-master-runbook.md:174 — violates: ADR-0040:33`

**Verdict:** pipeline health is not production-trustworthy: promote-by-digest has the right core digest-equality idea, but registry drift, bypassable gates, non-authoritative audit, broken prod deploy wiring, live GHCR/main residue, and missing fail-closed env wiring mean the dev→prod chain is currently easy to misdeploy or falsely attest.
